title: An operational AI bill of materials tracks models, prompts, data, tools and permissions
friendlyTitle: A useful AI inventory should record more than software packages
summary: A detailed white paper argues that an ordinary software bill of materials misses AI components that can change behavior without a code release, including hosted models, prompts, retrieval indexes, datasets and agent authority. It proposes a versioned dependency graph that separates supplier declarations from verified facts, internal assessments and runtime observations.
friendlySummary: AI systems also depend on models, prompts, search data, tools and permissions. The paper suggests recording how these parts connect, what version was used and whether each claim was checked or only supplied by a vendor.
whyItMatters: The approach turns AI inventory into an incident and change-management tool: teams can identify which systems used a retired model, compromised component or changed prompt and what must be retested. Even a small organization can start by recording model versions, prompt releases, data snapshots, tool permissions and explicit unknowns beside each production deployment.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A good map helps a team find affected systems when something changes or fails. Start by writing down the model, prompt, data source and tool access used by each important AI service.
